sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening heading and date for the maamar.

translations.translation: B"S.
The night of Erev Rosh HaShanah 5742*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The Tzemach Tzedek notes an apparent contradiction between Rosh HaShanah being the beginning of creation and merely a remembrance of the first day, and explains that both aspects exist, with the remembrance being loftier.

translations.translation: "This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day,"
and the Tzemach Tzedek
[the one whose birthday is on Erev Rosh HaShanah]
notes that there appears to be a contradiction from the beginning to the end,
for the meaning of "This day is the beginning of Your works"
(a literal beginning)
is that on Rosh HaShanah
(this day)
is the beginning of the coming into being of all the worlds,
meaning that on every Rosh HaShanah all worlds come into being anew
as they were the first time,
and the meaning of "a remembrance of the first day" is that Rosh HaShanah is only a remembrance of the first day.
And he explains regarding this,
that on Rosh HaShanah there are two matters,
that it is "the beginning of Your works" and that it is "a remembrance of the first day."
And from the fact that first we say that Rosh HaShanah is the beginning of Your works and afterwards we add that it is a remembrance of the first day,
it is proven
that this that Rosh HaShanah is a remembrance of the first day is more elevated
than that it is the beginning of Your works.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Rosh HaShanah is called the beginning of Your works because the purpose of creation—the revelation of G‑dliness—began with the creation of man, and the term "this day" indicates the ultimate revelation.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing the explanation of that which we say about the day of Rosh HaShanah, "This day is the beginning of Your works,"
for the question regarding this is well-known,
behold, on the twenty-fifth of Elul the world was created,
and Rosh HaShanah is the day when Adam, the first man, was created, which is the sixth day of creation, on which was the end and completion of creation,
so how can we say about this day that it is the beginning of Your works?
And the explanation of this is,
that the ultimate intent of the creation of the world is that there should be a revelation of G‑dliness within it,
to the extent that through every single detail of creation the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, will be revealed,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said
(at the conclusion and seal of tractate Avot)
"Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created only for His glory."
And this revelation is accomplished through the service of man.
Therefore we say about the day of Rosh HaShanah, "This day is the beginning of Your works,"
for this matter
(that there should be a revelation of G‑dliness in the world),
which is the intention of "Your works,"
began on the day when man was created.
For in addition to the fact that it was then that the possibility for a revelation of G‑dliness in the world was made,
it was then also actualized,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said
that Adam, the first man,
(on the day he was created)
proclaimed to all the creations, "Come,
let us bow down and prostrate ourselves, let us kneel before Hashem, our Maker,"
and they all answered and said, "Hashem
reigns, He is clothed in grandeur."
And it can be said,
that this that we say "This day is the beginning of Your works"
(although Rosh HaShanah is seemingly only the beginning of the intention of Your works),
is,
because "works" (maaseh) indicates completion,
for just as in man the completion of any matter is specifically when it comes into actuality,
so too is it above
[and moreover,
from this it is drawn down to lower man as well,
"man is an image of the supernal"],
that the completion of the entire order of Hishtalshelus is specifically in Asiyah.
And this is "This day is the beginning of Your works,"
for "works" indicates completion,
that the day of Rosh HaShanah, the day when Adam, the first man, was created,
is the beginning of the completion of creation.
And it can be said that this is also the reason that Rosh HaShanah is called here
(in continuation of "the beginning of Your works")
by the name "this day,"
for "this day" is revelation in the ultimate sense
["this" indicates revelation,
like one who points with his finger and says "this,"
and "day" indicates revelation,
as it is written,
"And G‑d called the light day,"
and "this day"
(two expressions of revelation)
is the ultimate revelation],
and this is "This day is the beginning of Your works,"
that this that Rosh HaShanah is the beginning of Your works,
the beginning of the completion of creation,
is that then the matter of revelation began
(for through the service of Adam, the first man, a revelation of G‑dliness was made in the world,
as above),
this matter of "this day."
